text: What, if any, impact the modality of aerobic training has on hypertrophic adaptations is unclear. The vast majority of studies on the topic to date have involved cycling exercise, and most of these trials have shown increased muscle protein accretion with consistent training. Studies using noncycling activities have produced mixed results. The previously mentioned study by Schwartz and colleagues (63) found increased muscle mass in elderly but not young male subjects following 6 months of a walk/jog/run protocol. In a study of elderly women, Sipila and Suominen (66) showed that a combination of step aerobics and track walking at intensities up to 80% of HRR did not significantly increase muscle cross-sectional area after 18 weeks of training.
